html:
Omar al-Bashir was the military ruler and president of Sudan from his coup on 30 June 1989 until he was overthrown on 11 April 2019.

He seized power with the backing of Hassan al-Turabi's Islamists, imposed strict Islamic rule, and hosted Osama bin Laden in the early 1990s, which brought United States sanctions. Oil exports from 1999 brought money. He later broke with Turabi.

His government fought the south until the peace of 2005, and in Darfur armed the Janjaweed militias. In 2009 the International Criminal Court charged him with war crimes and later genocide, the first such warrant for a sitting head of state. The revolution of 2019 ended his rule in Sudan.
sum: Omar al-Bashir was the military ruler and president of Sudan from his coup on 30 June 1989 until he was overthrown on 11 April 2019.
